title: Porto
lede: Three days built from thirteen saved reels — Lello at opening, oysters at the market, a Gaia sunset, the coast by tram, the six bridges by boat at golden hour, and one tasting menu.

base.label: Home base
base.name: Airbnb
base.address: Rua de Mouzinho da Silveira 105, 4050-265 Porto
base.q: Rua de Mouzinho da Silveira 105, Porto
base.note: The street runs from São Bento station down to the Ribeira: 3 min to the station, 5 to the river, 8 to Clérigos. Almost everything is on foot.

facts.label: Cash
facts.value: Carry some — small cafés prefer it

days.title: Arrive by rail, sunset, bacalhau
days.intro: Train day. The Alfa Pendular ends at Campanhã; a five-minute urban train, included in your ticket, drops you inside São Bento, three minutes from the door. Everything tonight is within ten minutes of the flat — Alibi, Emotivo and the market are closed on Sundays anyway.

stops.name: Arrive at Porto Campanhã
stops.what: The Alfa Pendular from Lisbon ends here, 3 km east of the centre — not at São Bento.
stops.why: Campanhã is where every long-distance train stops; the last hop into town is a five-minute urban train, and it's included in your ticket.
stops.logistics: Follow signs for 'Urbanos / São Bento'. On a Sunday a train leaves every 10–20 min; most Aveiro, Braga, Guimarães and Marco services end at Porto-São Bento — check the boards. Keep your Lisbon ticket: it's valid for this leg if you use it straight away.

stops.name: Urban train → São Bento
stops.what: Five minutes, one stop, free with your ticket.
stops.why: São Bento is three minutes from the door — and you step off the train straight into the azulejo hall, the best arrival in Porto. A taxi takes longer by the time you've found the rank.
stops.logistics: If the next train is 20 min away: Bolt/Uber 10 min, €7–10 — your street is cobbled and sloped, but it's three minutes with wheeled bags. The metro also works (Campanhã → Trindade, change to line D → São Bento, ~20 min) but it's more stairs with luggage.

stops.name: São Bento Station — the azulejo hall
stops.what: 20,000 tiles telling Portugal's history around the entrance hall. Ten minutes with the bags is enough.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'visit even if you're not taking a train' — you are taking one, and you arrive inside it. Late Sunday afternoon is quieter than any weekday morning, and you'll walk through again on Wednesday on the way out.

stops.name: Check in, drop bags
stops.what: Rua de Mouzinho da Silveira 105 — three minutes downhill from the station.
stops.why: Forty minutes to unpack and reset before the light goes.
stops.q: Rua de Mouzinho da Silveira 105, Porto

stops.name: Rua das Flores → Miradouro da Vitória
stops.what: Porto's prettiest street starts a minute from the door; follow it up and cut across to the terrace at Miradouro da Vitória — the whole Ribeira, the bridge and Gaia's cellars below you.
stops.why: The train gave you an hour back, and sunset is 18:55: this is the closest viewpoint to the flat that looks over the river for it. Not from your reels — skip it if you'd rather unpack slowly.
stops.logistics: 15 min of gentle uphill. The terrace is scruffy; the view isn't. From there it's 8 min down the steps to the quay.

stops.name: Ribeira quay & the Luís I lower deck
stops.what: Blue hour on the river. Walk halfway across the lower deck for the view and come back.
stops.why: The sun has just gone and the bridge lights come on while you're there. Reel 3 warns the Ribeira is packed by late morning; a Sunday evening in October is calm.
stops.logistics: 8 min down the steps from the viewpoint, or 5 min from the flat. No tickets, no plan.

stops.name: Bacalhau — Portuguese Wine & Food
stops.what: Bacalhau à Gomes de Sá (the Porto original), cod-skin chips, their 'bacalhau dourado'. Terrace on the river.
stops.why: The only restaurant from your reels that is both open on Sunday and five minutes from the door — exactly what a travel day needs.
stops.logistics: Open daily 12:00–22:00. Walk-ins normally; in the low season they take phone bookings — call from the train for a table for three. Backup if full: Meia-Nau (reel 12), seafood rice, open Sunday, 15 min away.
stops.q: Bacalhau Restaurante, Muro dos Bacalhoeiros 154, Porto

stops.name: Early night
stops.why: Monday starts at 08:20 — the bookshop opens at nine.

days.title: Lello at opening → Bolhão oysters → the river → Gaia sunset
days.intro: A loop: the bookshop and the tower before the crowds, downhill through the market to the river, across the bridge to Gaia, sunset, and back across to dinner — reel 3's tips in the order the geography wants them.

stops.name: Coffee on Rua das Flores
stops.what: Any café — 1 min from the door.
stops.why: A quick one — the bookshop opens at 09:00 and you want to be near the front of the line.

stops.name: Up past São Bento to Lello
stops.what: Three minutes up to the station, then Rua dos Clérigos — 10 min in all.
stops.why: A second look at the tiles, this time with a weekday crowd of commuters, on the way to the queue.

stops.name: Queue at Livraria Lello
stops.what: The 09:00 slot — the first of the day. Forty minutes inside.
stops.why: Reel 5's trick was the last slot at 19:00, but Tuesday evening now belongs to the boat and Emotivo. Opening is the other quiet window: the first group in gets ten minutes of the staircase before the shop fills, which doesn't happen again until closing. Be at the door ten minutes early.
stops.book: Buy 3 tickets for the 09:00 slot at livrarialello.pt
stops.logistics: Rua das Carmelitas 144, 9 min from São Bento. Open daily 09:00–19:30. The ticket's price comes off any book you buy. Slots sell out — buy now and check the time printed on the confirmation.

stops.name: Torre dos Clérigos
stops.what: 240 steps; the whole Baixa, the river and Gaia laid out below.
stops.why: Reel 3 says evening, but your evenings are spoken for — Gaia's sunset tonight, the boat tomorrow. At 09:45 the tower has just opened, the stairwell is empty, and the sun is behind you over the city, which is the light you want for the Ribeira side.
stops.logistics: Open 09:00–19:00, about €10 with the museum, no booking. Two minutes from Lello.

stops.name: Capela das Almas
stops.what: The blue-tiled chapel on Rua de Santa Catarina.
stops.why: Reel 3 lists it among the places 'crowded by late morning'. At 10:35 you're still ahead of the tour groups, which arrive from about 11.
stops.logistics: 15-min walk via Praça da Liberdade and Rua de Santa Catarina.

stops.name: Mercado do Bolhão
stops.what: Porto's oldest market. Wander the fish, flower and cheese stalls, then Rua de Santa Catarina next door.
stops.why: Open Mon–Sat 8–20 and closed Sunday, so it had to be a weekday — and the stalls are fullest before noon.
stops.logistics: 3 min. Forty minutes to browse, then straight to the oysters.

stops.name: Casa das Ostras
stops.what: Oysters from their own beds near Aveiro, shellfish with parsley olive oil, a glass of wine — under €30.
stops.why: Early lunch on purpose: only a handful of counter seats, and the market lunch rush peaks at 13:00. At 11:30 you walk straight in.
stops.logistics: Stalls 168–169 inside the market. No booking.
stops.q: Casa das Ostras, Mercado do Bolhão, Porto

stops.name: Down to the Ribeira
stops.what: Via Rua de Santa Catarina and Rua das Flores, or the Funicular dos Guindais down from Batalha.
stops.why: Downhill all the way, and there's no rush: the river cruise moved to Tuesday, so the Ribeira gets a slow hour instead.
stops.logistics: 20 min on foot, or the funicular down (~€4).

stops.name: The Ribeira at lunchtime
stops.what: Praça da Ribeira, the arcades, the rabelo boats, a coffee or a glass of something on the quay.
stops.why: Reel 3 warns it's packed by late morning — true, and this is the one time it's worth being in the crowd: full sun on the façades, the bridge above you, and the Gaia cellars across the water that you're about to visit.
stops.logistics: No plan here. If oysters weren't enough lunch, Taxca (reel 13) is 12 min back up the hill, or there's always a tosta on the quay.

stops.name: Funicular dos Guindais — up
stops.what: Three minutes from the river up to Batalha.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'take the funicular instead of climbing — it saves your legs and offers beautiful views of the river.' You need the top level for the upper deck anyway.
stops.logistics: ~€4. The base is at the east end of the quay, under the bridge.

stops.name: Luís I Bridge — upper deck, on foot
stops.what: Cross the top deck to Gaia.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'most tourists only take photos from one side — walking across gives the best views.' Mid-afternoon the sun is behind you, lighting the Ribeira façades.
stops.logistics: 7 min from Batalha to the deck, 10 min across.

stops.name: Gaia cable car — down
stops.what: Five minutes floating over the cellar rooftops to the quay.
stops.why: You land at the top station anyway. Buy the return — you'll ride back up for sunset.
stops.logistics: €10 return, no booking. Runs 10:00–19:00 until Oct 24.

stops.name: Cais de Gaia
stops.what: Rabelo boats and the postcard view back at Porto.
stops.why: Forty-five slow minutes before the tasting: the rabelo boats, the riverside, a pastel de nata.
stops.q: Cais de Gaia, Vila Nova de Gaia

stops.name: Port cellar tour & tasting
stops.what: A one-hour tour and tasting at a riverside house.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'don't skip Vila Nova de Gaia — the famous port wine cellars.' A 16:00 slot sits neatly between the cable car and sunset.
stops.logistics: Pick a riverside cellar so you don't lose time climbing: Cálem is at the cable-car base, Sandeman 3 min along; Taylor's and Graham's have the views but are 15–20 min uphill (the houses themselves aren't from your reels). About €20–25, English tours hourly.
stops.q: Caves Cálem, Vila Nova de Gaia

stops.name: Cable car up → Jardim do Morro
stops.what: Golden hour from about 18:15, sunset at 18:55.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'one of the best free sunset spots in Portugal.' Arriving by 17:45 gets you a spot on the grass before the crowd.
stops.logistics: Last cable car is 19:00 — you're up well before. There's a kiosk for a drink.
stops.q: Jardim do Morro, Vila Nova de Gaia

stops.name: Back across the upper deck
stops.what: The bridge and both banks lit up.
stops.why: Fifteen minutes of the best night view in the city, on the way to dinner.
stops.logistics: Upper deck → Sé → Rua dos Caldeireiros, 15–18 min.

stops.name: Alibi by YoursPorto
stops.what: Oysters and tuna tartare, then the Portuguese rice pots. Dessert and a glass of Port. Hidden courtyard at the back.
stops.why: Closed Sundays, open Mon–Sat 19:00–23:45 — so Monday it is, and it's on your walk home. If lunch was already oysters, go straight to the rice.
stops.logistics: Rua dos Caldeireiros 135. The flat is 6 min downhill.
stops.q: Alibi by YoursPorto, Rua dos Caldeireiros 135, Porto

days.title: Coast by tram, Matosinhos fish, the art district, six bridges at golden hour, a tasting menu
days.intro: The calendar forces this day: Dom Peixe and most galleries are closed on Mondays, Emotivo is Tue–Sat, and the boat is booked for 17:00. The afternoon drifts west — galleries, wine, a vintage tram down to the river — and the boat hands you back to the city at sunset.

stops.name: Breakfast near the flat
stops.why: Eat properly — lunch is at 12:15 after a long walk.

stops.name: Tram 1 from 'Infante' to Foz
stops.what: The historic tram along the river to Passeio Alegre, 25 min. Look left around the Arrábida bridge: the small Cais do Ouro pier there is where your boat leaves this afternoon.
stops.why: Reel 3: 'the historic trams are for the experience, not transport — charming but slow at busy hours.' First trams run about 09:00–09:30, every 20 min; this early you get a window seat.
stops.logistics: The stop is 5 min from the flat, beside Igreja de São Francisco. €6 cash on board.

stops.name: Foz do Douro promenade
stops.what: Passeio Alegre → Felgueiras lighthouse → the pergola → north along the beaches.
stops.why: Morning on the Atlantic before the city fills up. Reel 3: 'surprisingly windy — bring a light jacket, even in summer.'
stops.logistics: 60–75 min of walking.

stops.name: On to Matosinhos
stops.what: Keep walking the beach boardwalk (3 km, ~40 min) or hop on bus 500 along the coast (10 min).
stops.why: Aim to reach the restaurant right at opening.

stops.name: Dom Peixe
stops.what: Grilled fish sold by weight on Matosinhos' grill street.
stops.why: Closed Mondays, open Tuesday 12–23 — hence today. Arriving at 12:15 beats the local lunch rush at 13:00. Reel 6: 'Portugal's freshest seafood.'
stops.logistics: Rua Heróis de França 241. No booking needed at opening — a table for three is easy at 12:15.
stops.q: Dom Peixe, Rua Heróis de França 241, Matosinhos

stops.name: Metro line A → Lapa
stops.what: Blue line from Mercado or Matosinhos Sul, about 25 min.
stops.why: Fastest way back toward the art district.
stops.logistics: 10-min walk from Lapa station to Miguel Bombarda.

stops.name: Rua de Miguel Bombarda — the art district
stops.what: Galleries, makers, concept stores, the CC Bombarda arcade.
stops.why: Galleries open in the afternoon, mostly Tue–Sat from about 14:30 — a Monday visit would have found half of them shut. Reel 10's 'Porto for artists & designers'. Barro (reel 11) is on this street if you want a landmark.
stops.logistics: An hour and a quarter is enough. Leave by 15:45 to make the tram.

stops.name: Rua de Cedofeita → Garrafeira Oli Portugal
stops.what: The pedestrian shopping street leads south to local André's go-to wine shop.
stops.why: Buy today, not Wednesday — shops open around 10:00 and you'll be gone. They'll wrap bottles for the suitcase; you'll be carrying them onto a boat, so two is plenty.
stops.logistics: 15-min walk down the pedestrian street. Open Mon–Fri 10:00–21:00 (their site; another listing says 20:00). The Carmo tram stop is 3 min from the shop.
stops.q: Garrafeira Oli Portugal, Rua de Cedofeita 12, Porto

stops.name: Tram 18 from 'Carmo' → Cais do Ouro
stops.what: The other vintage tram: down Rua da Restauração to Massarelos, then west along the river. Get off at the Arrábida bridge — about 20 min.
stops.why: It leaves Carmo at :15 and :45, and the 16:15 drops you at the pier with twenty minutes to spare — a tram to your boat instead of a taxi. Miss it and take a Bolt from Carmo (10 min, €6–8); don't wait for the 16:45.
stops.logistics: Terminus beside Igreja do Carmo. €6 on board (card or MBway) or Andante. Tell the driver 'Cais do Ouro, Ponte da Arrábida'. Walking is 35 min, downhill — only if you left Bombarda early.

stops.name: Six bridges by boat — booked
stops.what: Douro In Board's small boat (ten aboard at most): up the river under all six bridges and back, with white and tawny Port, biscuits and water on board. 1 h 40 — back on the quay around 18:40.
stops.why: Fixed, because it's booked — and the slot is a gift. You're on the water for the whole golden hour, Ribeira and Gaia glowing on either side, and you dock as the sun drops into the river mouth (sunset 18:55). Reel 3's 'book in advance' box is ticked.
stops.book: Booked — Viator, 3 adults. Show the mobile ticket.
stops.logistics: Meeting point: Rua do Ouro 180 — the small Cais do Ouro pier beside the Arrábida bridge, where the Afurada river taxi leaves. Be there by 16:45. It's a tiny operator: if nobody's there at 17:05, call the number on the Viator confirmation (one review mentions a no-show). Free cancellation until 24 h before. Bring a layer — it's cooler on the water after 18:00.

stops.name: Back to town
stops.what: Bolt or Uber from the pier: 10 min to the flat to freshen up, or 12 min straight to Emotivo.
stops.why: Dinner is at 20:00 and the pier is 3 km west of the flat — a ride is €6–9 and buys you half an hour at home first.
stops.logistics: Cheaper: bus 500 toward Praça da Liberdade from the riverside stop (every 15–20 min, about 15 min to the Alfândega), then 10 min uphill. Walking is 40 min — not tonight.
stops.q: Rua de Mouzinho da Silveira 105, Porto

stops.name: Walk to Cedofeita
stops.what: 15 min, uphill at first.
stops.why: The room is small — don't be late.

stops.name: Emotivo
stops.what: A seven-moment tasting menu of two Portuguese regions (they change every two months). €90 per two people, excluding drinks.
stops.why: Tue–Sat only, 19:00–24:00 — tonight is your one chance. Reel 8: 'the #1 place I needed to go in Porto.' A 20:00 table gives you about two hours. Last night, best meal.
stops.logistics: Rua do Rosário 124. The menu is written for two — say you're three when you book and ask how they handle an odd table (usually fine). The flat is 15 min downhill.

alternates.name: Barro
alternates.note: Garlic prawns and sharing plates, on Miguel Bombarda — if Emotivo falls through.
alternates.q: Barro, Rua de Miguel Bombarda 38, Porto

alternates.name: Taxca
alternates.note: Bifanas and petiscos in the Baixa — if you skip Matosinhos and want a quick city lunch.

days.title: Out by noon
days.intro: Short and calm. The tiles are on the way out.

stops.name: Pack, then coffee and a pastel de nata on Rua das Flores
stops.why: One minute from the door, and nothing else opens before you leave.

stops.name: Leave the flat → São Bento
stops.what: 3 min uphill. The metro entrance is in the station building.
stops.why: One last five minutes with the azulejos on the way out.
stops.logistics: Metro D → Trindade (one stop) → line E → Aeroporto, about 40 min door to door. Or Uber/Bolt, 20–25 min.

stops.name: At the airport for the 12:00 flight
stops.why: 2 h 45 before departure — right for a US-bound flight with non-Schengen exit passport control. Flying within Europe? Leaving the flat at 09:00 is fine.

planB.title: Plan B — if the Douro Valley is non-negotiable
planB.text: With the boat booked for 17:00 on Tuesday, the valley only fits as a long Monday: the early train São Bento → Pinhão (about 2 h 20, €12–14 each way, sit on the right, scenic after Régua), lunch and a quinta tasting, and the mid-afternoon train back to be at Jardim do Morro for sunset. You'd give up Lello, the market oysters, the bridge walk, the cable car and the cellar tour — too much to trade on a two-day visit, which is why it's Plan B. The boat you booked is the Douro on the water; save the valley for a return trip. If you do go, check departures on cp.pt (4–6 trains a day, no seat reservations).

bookings.what: Six-bridges boat — Douro In Board via Viator, 3 adults
bookings.when: Booked ✓ — be at Rua do Ouro 180 by 16:45
Now — small room; the menu is priced per two, ask how they seat three

bookings.what: Port cellar tour for 3, English (e.g., Cálem or Sandeman)

noBooking: No booking needed: Casa das Ostras and Dom Peixe (arrive at opening), the cable car, the funicular, both trams, the Clérigos tower.

walking.place: Cais do Ouro pier — don't walk

bench.name: Pronto Breakfast
bench.why: Sunday-only pop-up, 8–15. Your only Sunday is arrival evening.

bench.name: Spiritus light show
bench.why: Reel 3's 'light show after 6 PM' inside the Clérigos church. It lost its slot to the boat, and Monday's 18:00 is the Gaia sunset. Next trip.

bench.name: Taxca · Casa Expresso · O Golfinho · Solar Moinho de Vento
bench.why: Baixa tascas; only two lunches and they went to the oysters and the Matosinhos fish. Taxca is the easiest swap-in.

bench.name: Barro · Pata Gorda · Meia-Nau
bench.why: Only two dinners after arrival night. Barro and Meia-Nau are the Tuesday alternates; Pata Gorda is out in Foz with unreliable hours.

bench.name: GetYourGuide food tips · MAD House creative guide
bench.why: Their places are only shown on video; covered in spirit by Bolhão and Miguel Bombarda.
